appraisal_events.evidence: Croyez-vous que la salive envenimée de cinq cents petits bonshommes de vos amis, juchés les uns sur les autres, arriverait à baver seulement jusqu'à mes augustes orteils?
appraisal_events.explanation: Charlus escalates into a furious self-glorifying tirade dismissing the narrator and his friends as beneath contempt, though the narrator's own description of his 'augustes orteils' and mock-deification frames the outburst with clear irony.

appraisal_events.evidence: je me précipitai sur le chapeau haut de forme neuf du baron, je le jetai par terre, je le piétinai... Ma colère n'avait pas calmé celle du baron, ma sortie de la chambre parut lui causer une vive douleur, il me rappela, me fit rappeler... il courut à toutes jambes, me rattrapa dans le vestibule et me barra la porte. « Allons, me dit-il, ne faites pas l'enfant, rentrez une minute »
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator's explosive defiance -- destroying Charlus's hat and storming out -- reverses the dynamic: Charlus, moments earlier all-powerful, now anxiously chases and appeases him.

status_effects.explanation: His tirade still commands the scene through sheer volume and rhetorical excess, though the narrator's ironic framing of his self-deification tempers the effect.
By finally acting on his fury and walking out, the narrator forces Charlus into an anxious, pursuing, conciliatory posture, a marked reversal from his earlier total passivity.
His fury dissolves into anxious pursuit and tender appeasement, revealing a dependency on the narrator that undercuts his earlier claim of total superiority.
